title: Figure AI
summary:
Figure AI, Inc. is an American robotics company developing AI-powered humanoid robots. The company was founded in 2022 by Brett Adcock, also known for founding Archer Aviation and Vettery. Adcock assembled Figure's team from people working at Boston Dynamics, Tesla, Google DeepMind, and Apple.

In 2022, the company introduced its prototype, Figure 01, a bipedal robot designed for manual labor. On August 6, 2024, Figure AI introduced Figure 02, described as the next step toward deploying humanoids for industrial use, featuring integrated cabling in its limbs, a battery integrated into the torso, and 6 RGB cameras paired with an onboard vision language model. On October 9, 2025, Figure AI introduced Figure 03, a complete hardware and software redesign aimed at creating a general-purpose robot capable of learning directly from humans, with upgraded cameras delivering double the frame rate, one-quarter the latency, and a 60% wider field of view. The redesigned five-fingered robotic hands have 16 degrees of freedom and can carry objects up to 25kg.

Helix is an evolved version featuring Helix VLA, a generalist vision-language-action neural network that can observe surroundings, respond to natural language commands, and interact with the real world without extended training. With a third round of financing in September 2025 amounting to $1 billion, the company's total valuation rose to $39 billion. Investors included Intel, Nvidia, Qualcomm, T-Mobile, Salesforce, and Brookfield Asset Management.

On March 15, 2025, Figure AI introduced BotQ, a manufacturing facility aiming to produce 12,000 humanoids per year, with plans to progressively use its own humanoid robots to assist in building additional robots. Figure 02 robots have been tested at a BMW plant in South Carolina.
